transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. It's, um, it's really nice to meet you. Thank you for seeing me. I hope I can be helpful today. 

I guess... well, they told me I needed to come in because of some stuff happening at work, down at the warehouse. I'm a really hard worker, I promise, it's just... I guess I've been doing some things that bother the other guys, and I feel really bad about it. Like, sometimes I'll just sort of... freeze, with my arms up in the air by the forklift. I don't really mean to cause a problem. And I guess I catch myself copying the backing-up beeping sounds it makes, or doing the hand signals the drivers use. 

And, um... sometimes I just need to move the freight boxes into these... these specific little patterns. It's nothing bad, but everyone starts yelling for me to stop and get back to the normal loading. I'm really trying to do better and not upset my boss, though. Is... is it okay that I'm explaining it like this?
Before you freeze, make the beeping sounds, or copy the hand signals, do you notice a build-up of tension or an urge that feels relieved once you do it?

Um... no, not really. I don't think so, anyway. It's not like... like when you really need to stretch or something and then you feel better after. I don't feel any tension at all, I promise. 

It's more like... I just sort of realize I'm already doing it, or my body just kind of... stops. I don't even really think about it beforehand. I hope that's okay to say? I know that probably sounds weird, and I really don't want to be difficult or give you the wrong answer. I just... I don't feel an urge first. Is that... does that make sense for what you were asking?
Have you been doing things like this—freezing in position, repeating sounds, or arranging objects in patterns—since you were a child, or did this start more recently as a new change for you?

Oh, um... no, not since I was little. I was always a really good kid, I promise, I never caused any trouble like this back then. This is... it's a newer thing. 

I'd say the... the strange behavior at the warehouse, and I guess sometimes the guys say my talking gets a little confusing for them... it's really only been happening for about six months now. So it hasn't been forever or anything. I really hope that doesn't make me sound too bad or, you know, broken. I've only been messing up at work for those last six months, so I'm really hoping I can just fix it and get back to how I used to be. 

Is... is six months the kind of timeline you were looking for? I hope I'm answering your questions right.
Have you noticed yourself hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or having beliefs that others have told you aren't true, around the same time these episodes started?

Oh, um... no. No, I don't hear any voices or sounds like that. I promise. I know sometimes people who have trouble fitting in might... might have those kinds of things, but my mind is pretty quiet. 

And I don't think I have any weird beliefs, either. I just... I just believe in trying to do a good job and being helpful to the other guys. I haven't been arguing with anyone about what's true or anything like that. 

I really hope it's okay that I don't have that? I don't want to mess up your evaluation by not having the right answers for you, but I want to be completely honest. I'm not crazy or anything scary, I'm just having those weird habits I mentioned. Is... is that a good sign, that I don't hear voices?
Have you had any recent medical problems, head injuries, infections, or been using any new medications, drugs, or alcohol around the time these behaviors started?

Oh, um... no, sir. No medical problems or head injuries or anything like that. I've always been pretty healthy, honestly. And I definitely don't use drugs or drink too much. I mean, maybe a beer with the guys after a shift every once in a while, but nothing crazy, I promise. I know how important it is to stay clean, especially working in the warehouse. 

I haven't taken any new medicines either. Just... just the usual stuff if I get a headache, like Tylenol. 

I hope that's okay? I just want you to know I'm not doing anything bad to myself to cause this. I'm really trying to be a good patient for you. Does... does that help rule some things out?

You mentioned that your coworkers say your talking gets confusing sometimes—can you tell me more about that? For example, do you find your thoughts jumping around, or do others have trouble following the connection between what you say?

Oh, um... yeah, I guess that does happen sometimes. I don't mean for it to, I really don't. I try so hard to be clear. But... well, like, if my supervisor asks me which pallets are supposed to go on the truck, I... I start trying to explain it to him, like a good worker should. But then my words just sort of... slip? 

I'll start talking about the load sheet, and then somehow I'm talking about my old house, and then fishing, and... and then church boxes. And by the time I stop talking, nobody has any idea what I meant. 

I'm really sorry, I know that sounds terrible and like I'm not paying attention. But I promise I am! It's just... my brain gets a little too fast, maybe? I really hope my supervisor isn't too mad at me. I'm trying to do better, I swear. Is... is it normal to get a little mixed up like that sometimes? I hope it doesn't make me seem like a bad employee.

Over these past six months, have you noticed any changes in your emotions or interest in things—like feeling less enjoyment from activities you used to like, or feeling emotionally flat or distant from people close to you?

Oh, um... no. No, I don't think so. I still care about things, I promise! I still like, you know, hanging out with the guys at the warehouse during break, and... and I still enjoy my regular stuff. 

I try really hard to be friendly and upbeat with everyone. I always make sure to smile and ask people how their day is going so they know I'm paying attention to them. I definitely don't feel flat or distant from anybody. 

I really hope it's okay that my emotions are still pretty normal? I don't want to sound like I'm not taking your questions seriously, but I really do try to just be a positive person. Does... does that sound like a good thing to you?
During those times you freeze with your arms up, if someone tries to move your arms or reposition you, do you resist them, or does your body stay stiff, or does it move easily like it's pliable?

Oh, um... you mean when I get stuck? Honestly, nobody's really tried to push me or move me when that happens. Usually, if I'm at the warehouse, the guys just kind of... walk around me, or they wait for me to snap out of it. I try really hard not to be in anyone's way when it happens, I promise! 

I don't think I'd fight anybody if they tried to move me, though. I'm not a difficult person, I swear. I always try to cooperate with whatever people need me to do. I just... I get kind of locked up, I guess? But I'm not trying to be stubborn or anything. 

I really hope that's an okay answer? I just don't want you to think I'm being aggressive or unhelpful when I freeze up. I really am trying my best to just be normal. Does that make sense?

Have you noticed yourself laughing, smiling, or reacting emotionally in ways that don't seem to match what's actually happening around you—like giggling during a serious conversation or feeling amused by something upsetting?

Oh, no, I don't think I do that. I mean, I really try to be respectful when people are talking to me, especially if it's something serious. I would never want to laugh if someone was upset or talking about something sad. That would be so rude, and I really try hard to be polite to everyone. 

Sometimes I might smile just because I'm trying to be friendly, you know? Like, I just want people to know I'm listening and that I'm a nice guy. But I definitely don't giggle at bad things. I always try to react the right way. 

I hope that's what you were asking? I just really want to make sure I'm doing things right and not upsetting anyone. I'm a good listener, I promise.

Besides the freezing episodes, have you noticed times when you refuse to speak at all, resist doing what others ask even though you could do it, or feel a sudden urge to move around excessively without any real purpose?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean... I always talk to people when they talk to me. I'm a really good communicator, I promise! If someone asks me to do something at work, like move a pallet or stack some boxes, I do it right away. I would never just refuse to do my job or ignore people. I want my boss and the guys to know I'm reliable. 

And I don't just run around for no reason, either. I mean, I stay busy at the warehouse because there's always stuff to move, but I'm just doing my job, you know? I'm not hyper or anything like that. I try really hard to just do what I'm supposed to do and be helpful.

I really hope that's okay? I just want you to know I'm a good worker and I try to do everything right. I'm not trying to be difficult or weird or anything. Does that sound like a good answer?
Over these past six months, have you noticed any changes in your ability to keep up with daily routines, like bathing, dressing, or maintaining your living space, compared to before?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I still take showers and everything! I try really hard to stay clean, especially because working at the warehouse gets you pretty sweaty and dusty. I always want to make sure I don't smell bad around the other guys. That would be awful, right? 

And my apartment is... well, it's fine! I mean, I'm a single guy, so maybe it's a little messy sometimes, like a few dishes in the sink or some laundry in a basket, but it's not dirty or anything. I try to keep it nice. I always make sure to wear clean clothes to work, too. I want to look presentable and show I take my job seriously. 

I really try to keep up with everything. I'm doing a good job with all that, I think? I hope you don't think I'm letting myself go or anything. I'm trying really hard to just be a normal, responsible guy. Is that the kind of thing you were wondering about?
